originality.rationale: The exact leading collision constant for two random binary strings with identical ordered two-mer multispectra is not stated in the inspected relevant primary papers or closest published published-finding corpus files. The published per-profile formula does imply an exact finite summation, but not the proved leading constant without an additional nontrivial two-dimensional Fourier saddle analysis that treats the two lattice saddle points and endpoint-flow classes. Novelty remains qualified by the possibility of an unindexed Markov-type collision asymptotic.
residual_risks: Unindexed information-theory or Markov-type collision literature may contain the same asymptotic constant.

value.rationale: A canonical natural collision probability measures average confusability of two independent strings from complete shortest nontrivial ordered-read spectra. The sharp constant gives the leading additive term of the Rényi-2 information of the readout. Unlike known profile counts or individual class sizes, it quantifies the aggregate probabilistic ambiguity, including a nontrivial parity/endpoints contribution; it is a motivated asymptotic invariant with potential use in random reconstruction and collision estimates.
